indicator_definition: The adolescent birth rate is the number of live births per 1,000 women aged 15 to 19 years. It measures the prevalence of teenage pregnancies and reflects access to sexual and reproductive health education and services. Data are compiled from national vital statistics by Eurostat.
rationale: High adolescent birth rates are associated with increased health risks for mother and child, and with reduced educational and economic opportunities for young women. Reducing the adolescent birth rate requires access to comprehensive sexual education and reproductive health services. Progress means a sustained decrease in births to adolescent women.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled from national birth registrations and population statistics. The rate is calculated by dividing live births to women aged 15–19 by the total female population aged 15–19, multiplied by 1,000. Data are reported to Eurostat annually by national statistical authorities.
